endorsements.quote: Recommendation 2: Training data should be derived from a population that matches one’s population as closely as possible.
A clear articulation of the model development process, such as the source and quality of the training datasets, would increase confidence in the product.

It is essential to ensure that practicing clinicians are fully aware of the risks and limitations of AI products before implementing them, to ensure long-term successful adoption of AI solutions in clinical practice.

Recommendation 5: To mitigate risks of model drifts, it may be prudent for users to deploy “continuous learning” models alongside “locked” algorithms before implementation, introduce protocols to log model updates so that reversal is possible, and conduct more frequent reviews of model performance.

This will include establishing a governing body to regulate and supervise the use of AI tools in radiology and continuously monitor the safety of these tools throughout their clinical implementation [ 4 ].
Given the abundance and rapidly growing number of AI solutions in the market, it is prudent for users to prioritize clinical use cases that have the greatest impact on their clinical practice.

unlisted_practices: Conduct routine (e.g., yearly) performance reviews of deployed AI solutions and take the algorithm offline and rebuild it where necessary.
Critically review research papers on AI tools to identify gaps before adoption rather than accepting reported performance.
Validate vendor performance claims using locally annotated ground-truth datasets in a sandbox or staging environment separate from production systems.
Survey user needs and base AI integration on the clinical workflow before implementation.
Engage imaging informatics professionals to ensure seamless technical integration of AI models.
Ensure patient data privacy and security when using local or cloud-based AI inference.
Use explainability outputs such as heat maps to review whether features used for AI predictions are reasonable.
Ensure fair and equal access to and use of AI regardless of age, race, sex, income, social status, and ability to use technology.
Conduct large clinical trials and outcome-based studies before clinical implementation of AI tools.
Have radiologists test and trial market-ready AI solutions to gain experience and select applications suited to their workflow.
Mitigate federated learning cybersecurity vulnerabilities through encryption and differential privacy.
Require AI vendors to demonstrate real-world local efficacy beyond regulatory approval claims.
Address reimbursement and willingness-to-pay issues for sustained AI deployment.

screen.reason: This is a position statement paper offering recommendations and guidelines on the adoption and clinical deployment of AI in radiology.
